top.title: Paul George revenge game fuels Boston Celtics blowout of Philadelphia 76ers
top.description: In a game that many saw as a clash of the Eastern Conference titans currently at the top of the standings to start the 2026-27 NBA regular season, the reality was a 123-101 road blowout win for the Boston Celtics over the Philadelphia 76ers . The Celtics were in control for nearly the entire game, trailing by 1 point briefly before Boston blew it open in the final frame with a barrage of makes from beyond the arc. That the Celtics held the Sixers to just 30 percent from deep on a night they shot 45 percent from 3 helped quite a bit, as did winning the shot attempt battle 95-79. Oddly, Boston was awarded just 5 free throw attempts to Philly's 28, but forced 14 turnovers to their own 9. The win puts Boston in sole possession of the East's top spot, with the Celtics improving to 9-2 on the season to date. Listen to "What have we learned about the Celtics two weeks into the NBA season?" on Spreaker. Let's take a look at the best plays from the first matchup between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown since the latter's trade to the Sixers this summer captured in images. top.title: Oregon star edge rusher Teitum Tuioti out for the season
top.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Ducks senior defensive end Teitum Tuioti suffered a season-ending knee injury in Oregon’s 41-28 win over Ohio State , Dan Lanning announced on Monday. “Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year, and every year he’s been here,” Lanning said. “Just watching him grow as a player and person has been a lot of fun for us. But unfortunately Teitum’s done for the year, he had a knee injury, he’ll end up having surgery.” Tuioti was among the Ducks’ leaders in tackles with 44, and ranked second on the team in sacks with 5.5 on the season. The former Sheldon High School star sits at No. 8 all-time for Oregon with 22.5 sacks across his four seasons, providing steady leadership on a talented and experienced defensive front. In the win over the Buckeyes, he also showed off his arm: Tuioti completed a pass to fellow defensive end Matayo Uiagalelei on a memorable fake punt which shifted momentum in the game. “I hate it for him, because (the injury) was a routine, weird play that it happened on,” Lanning said. “He left it on the line there on the field, and I don’t know if he’ll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is gonna be really, really lucky.” Should Tuioti forgo his fifth year of eligibility and enter the NFL Draft, he is a projected second- or third-round pick according to some mock drafts. top.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
top.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. Morant tried to lay out a vision for how it could look. If he drives to the paint and is double-teamed, someone else is inevitably open. That’s how basketball works. “That allows me to have more space to be the best Ja I can be,” Morant said. top.title: Who will call plays for Oregon after Mehringer's firing?
top.description: EUGENE — After firing first-year offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer seven games into the 2026 season, Dan Lanning shared Oregon ’s plans for filling his role moving forward at his weekly press conference Monday night. Offensive assistant Jay Johnson will lead offensive playcalling for the Ducks going forward, Lanning said. “He has a lot of experience as a play-caller, was with me in Georgia when we were part of the national championship team,” Lanning said. “Went on to have a lot of success in Colorado and Michigan State. He’s gonna lead the efforts there with the offensive staff, but it’ll still be a collaborative effort, with a lot of the work that we do. “He’s also coming in with a different perspective, a different view, not being with us the last few years, where he can provide a couple things that might be different than what we’ve done.” Mehringer, previously the tight ends coach for the Ducks, is the first assistant coach Lanning has fired in his tenure at Oregon, which began in 2022. The Ducks’ offensive decision-making was at the center of intense criticism over the past three weeks, during which Oregon averaged just 14 points per game and lost twice to UCLA and Illinois. Lanning spoke to the human element of letting Mehringer go. “They see the football coach, right? That’s also an unbelievable dad. A great husband,” Lanning said. “The guy’s been part of our staff for the last five years, that’s done some really good things here, and I think all of us feel like we shoulder some of the blame. top.title: Lanning: Stewart incident 'didn't match our standard'
top.description: EUGENE — After Oregon wide receiver Evan Stewart was booked in Springfield Municipal Jail early Sunday morning on DUII charges, Ducks coach Dan Lanning addressed the situation at his weekly press conference Monday. “There was an incident this weekend that didn’t match our standard here in our program,” Lanning said. “There will be an appropriate action taken. Still gathering some details with what that situation looks like. But that would be handled internally. I’m not gonna respond to any other questions about that. We’re gonna handle that with our guys. “There’s an expectation of what you have to... how you have to act, and how you need to perform in our program. Kind of overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing, but that will be handled by us internally. I’m not going to speak on it publicly.” When Lanning was asked a follow-up question about a rumored speeding incident involving other Oregon football players, for which there haven’t been any confirmed arrests, he said, “I was talking about the same thing when I first addressed it.” This is also the second instance of an Oregon football team member facing DUII charges in the past year. In April, running backs coach Ra’Shaad Samples allegedly backed his Ford F-150 into a parked car outside a bar in Eugene. His next court date is Oct. 27. An arraignment for Stewart in his DUII case hasn’t been set, as official charges haven’t been filed to Springfield Municipal Court as of Monday evening, according to court records. Stewart leads the Ducks this season with 27 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns. He missed Saturday’s win over Nebraska due to an undisclosed injury. Oregon (4-2, 2-1 Big Ten) is preparing for a road game at Illinois (3-3, 1-2) at 12 p.m. PT this coming Saturday. top.title: Stephen A. Smith says Lakers can’t win a title with ‘top three players being white’
top.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers have been one of the NBA’s best teams to start the season, winning six straight games behind Luka Doncic. But Stephen A. Smith still isn’t buying them as a championship contender for a rather bizarre reason: their top players are all white. This week, the ESPN star claimed that he wasn’t sold on the Lakers winning a championship, pointing to the race of their top players. Smith said that he has “never seen an NBA team with its top three players being white” win a championship, and that “it ain’t gonna happen” this year. Lakers’ Hot Start The Lakers retooled their roster around Doncic this offseason. Along with Austin Reaves, they added center Walker Kessler in a July sign-and-trade with the Utah Jazz, sending multiple future first-round picks and pick swaps to Utah. The move has paid off so far. The Lakers have won six straight games, with Doncic putting up 32 points, eight rebounds, and 10 assists in his return to the lineup in a win over the Atlanta Hawks, per ESPN . Smith made a similar argument about the Lakers’ big three over the summer, and the comments drew plenty of backlash at the time. ‘It ain’t gonna happen’ While the Lakers may be off to a hot start this season, Smith made it clear that he hasn’t changed his mind. “I’ve never seen an NBA team with its top three players being white deliver a championship. It’s never happened. And I’m here to tell you, I don’t think it’s gonna happen this year,” Smith said, in a clip shared by Awful Announcing . After running through other contenders, Smith added, “Lakers got a chance. I just don’t think it’s going to materialize into a championship.” Smith insisted that he wasn’t making an issue of race, but was “just talking about the actual facts.” He then ran through a list of past champions, from the Larry Bird and Kevin McHale Boston Celtics to the Golden State Warriors. “You can bring up whoever the hell you want. There has never been in my lifetime an NBA team led with its top three players being white that delivered you a championship with an abundance of brothers playing basketball,” Smith said. Smith admitted that a title for Doncic would be big for the NBA, especially with the Olympics coming to Los Angeles in 2028. “It would be huge for the league. It would be huge for the Olympics. It would be huge for LA. It would be huge for everything, but it ain’t gonna happen. I can’t see it,” Smith said. “Not a team with its top three players being white dudes. I’m sorry, I think that’s controversial in some people’s eyes. It ain’t controversial in mine. I’m just telling you how it is. I’m calling it like I see it.” Clearly, the Lakers still have plenty to prove to Smith. The post Stephen A. top.title: Hawks fall short in OT to Virginia Tech, 93-88
top.description: SIOUX CITY, IOWA - NOVEMBER 10: Cooper Koch #8 of the Iowa Hawkeyes drives against Amani Hansberry #13 of the Virginia Tech Hokies during the second half at Tyson Events Center on November 10, 2026 in Sioux City, Iowa. (Photo by Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Iowa Hawkeyes (2-1) got slow starts in each of the three frames tonight in a 93-88 loss to Virginia Tech (3-0). The most notable was not scoring a field goal until 0:44 left in the overtime frame. Despite having a chance to tie at the end, Cooper Koch couldn’t make his 3 point attempt amidst a career night. Giving up 93 points is never Ben McCollum’s preferred style and they struggled to contain the Hokie guards, Ben Hammond & Jaylen Curry, who combined for 57 points on 18/34 shooting and 16/18 from the line. Curry’s 3 pointer in overtime proved to be enough distance for Tech as the Hawks couldn’t get it inside of 2 after that. It was a game riddled with fouls and the Hawks finished 66% (31/47) from the line. The biggest of which was Ty’reek Coleman missing on his final attempt with less than 2 seconds left in regulation. Andrew McKeever couldn’t convert the putback quick enough, which allowed VT to come away with the victory in Sioux City’s Tyson Center. The flipside of foul trouble was Kael Combs who lived in foul trouble for the bulk of the game with 2 early ones before the first television timeout, a third later in the first half, and a fourth right out of the break. Thankfully Coleman performed well off the bench with 20 points on 7/10 shooting. Career night for Cooper Koch Despite missing his final attempt of the game, Koch was aggressive all night, with 15/17 from the line en route to a career high 26 points. He was just 5/11 from the field and 1/5 from 3 but he played incredibly hard for all 45 minutes of the game. Many of his free throw attempts came on drives and post ups where he pulled out the Kevin Durant rip throw. Iowa will need to see him take more shots. Koch was joined in double digits by Coleman, Isaia Howard (13 on 3/5 from deep), and Combs (10 points on 4/4). Offensive rebounding kept the Hawks in it Iowa rebounded 18 of 35 opportunities, good for 18 second chance points. It came from unexpected sources – McKeever got his 3 but Coleman and Howard added 3 of their own. While Iowa went after size in the portal, much of the rebounding gains tonight happened from Iowa’s guards. High leverage free throw shooting hurts Iowa Coleman missed the second of 2 attempts down the stretch and then he & Koch combined for 3/5 in the extra frame. Any one of those misses very easily could have flipped it for Iowa. Overall the 31/47 is going to add some frustration to the loss but 7 of Iowa’s 16 misses came from Cam Manyawu & McKeever who went just 2/9. They’re not good FT shooters but they have to be better than that. Next up: Sunday, November 15th at 2:00p vs Creighton in Des Moines, IA

top.title: Louisville Defeats Lindenwood 71-35
top.description: Lindenwood came into the Yum and played hard for 4 quarters but the biggest suspense of the night was whether their coach, Phil Sayers, was going to put freshman Brynn Owens into the game. She had a large contingent of determined and loud fans from up the road in Indiana who got even the Louisville fans to chant for her to be played. Finally in the last few minutes of the game he gave the people what they wanted and there was much rejoicing. Tajianna Roberts led both teams in scoring with 15. Amiya Joyner had a double-double with 11 points and 10 rebounds. Mackenly Randolph should be cleared for the game on Thursday but Elif Istanbulluoglu returned to play after an ankle injury and had 5 rebounds and 2 points. Virginia Tech transfer Carys Baker came out of her shooting slump to finally get her 1000th point. She finished the game with 12 points and 5 rebounds. After the game Carys said, “For me obviously the last couple of games were hard just going scoreless but I think with my teammates they have so much confidence in me for me to be able to knock those down. Staying in the gym and staying positive I always want to be a team player so I didn’t let it affect me. Everyone was telling me to go out there and have fun, and I think that’s what I did.” Coach Walz said, “I thought our effort, especially on the defensive end, in the first half was extremely good. We played hard. We played focused. The second half we got a little carried away trying to steal it every time instead of having good fundamentals and trying to keep someone in front of us. We’ve got to get a lot better real quick at guarding the ball. We’re allowing way too many straight line drives and it’s going to be a problem.” He added, “I’m hoping we can improve without having to get our butts kicked and all of a sudden it’s an eye opener like oh sh*t he actually knows what he’s talking about.” Next up the Cards hit the road to play Ball State on Thursday. top.title: UCLA football makes stunning move in CFP rankings after initial snub
top.description: Given another week to assess UCLA, the College Football Playoff selection committee had a different take on the Bruins. Move them up. Way up. In the wake of an impressive road victory over Minnesota, UCLA rose to No. 4 in the CFP rankings released Tuesday night. That’s four spots above where the Bruins were slotted only a week ago . Most importantly, moving into the top four puts UCLA (9-0 overall, 6-0 Big Ten) on track to receive a first-round bye into the quarterfinal round of the 12-team playoff. UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against Minnesota in an NCAA college football game Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, in Minneapolis. AP Photo/Abbie Parr So, did the CFP selection committee make a mistake last week when it came to the Bruins? “I don’t think it was an admission of them being ranked too low,” Hunter Yurachek, chairman of the CFP selection committee, said on a conference call with reporters. “I think what we’re seeing with the parity around college football [is] that we now have only two remaining unbeaten teams and UCLA is one of those, and I think they continue to improve as a team. “The defense has been steady and really dominant all season, they’ve had an established running game and their quarterback play is getting better — their backup quarterback that has been filling in really seemed to find his way, especially in the fourth quarter of that game against Minnesota.” Notre Dame wide receiver Micah Gilbert (14) scores a touchdown during the second half of an NCAA college football game against Miami, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. AP Photo/Paul Barnick Yurachek was alluding to quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who replaced the injured Nico Iamaleava a month ago, throwing 75-yard touchdown passes on back-to-back offensive plays to help the Bruins pull away for a 34-20 victory over the Golden Gophers. This is UCLA’s highest spot ever in the CFP rankings after its No. 8 ranking last week tied its previous high from the 2014 season. The only teams ranked ahead of the Bruins were No. 1 Georgia, No. 2 Utah and No. 3 Alabama. UCLA and Utah are the last remaining unbeaten teams in major college football. The Bruins’ move was part of a major shakeup in which no team remained in the same CFP spot as a week ago. USC (7-2, 4-2) rose two spots to No. 18 and has a chance to vastly improve its standing Saturday when it faces No. 9 Indiana, which dropped five spots despite not playing last weekend. Should the Bruins secure a first-round bye, they’ll need to come up with a plan to avoid the fate of nearly every predecessor in that spot — teams with byes have gone only 1-7 in the quarterfinals since the playoff expanded to 12 teams for the 2024 season. Indiana’s Byron Baldwin Jr. (2) celebrates a victory against Minnesota during a football game at Memorial Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, 2026. top.title: Georgia ranked in no. 1 of second College Football Playoff rankings
top.description: The second edition of the 2026-27 College Football Playoff rankings was released on Nov. 10, and the Georgia Bulldogs earned their No. 1 spot in the rankings. They had a dominant 42-7 win against the Ole Miss Rebels, who were ranked a top-10 team by the College Football Playoff when Georgia faced them. The Bulldogs now have two wins against teams in the top 25 this week (No. 3 Alabama, now No. 19 Ole Miss). Week 11 will give the Bulldogs another team in the top 25: the No. 22 Missouri Tigers . They aren't as battle-tested as Ole Miss; Missouri lost at home to the No. 6 Texas Longhorns 34-20, and their strongest win of the year has been against a 5-4 Florida Gators team. However, with Georgia's loss to unranked Auburn earlier in the year, no game can be taken lightly. Speaking of the SEC, there are a lot of teams from the SEC that are currently in a spot in the College Football Playoff. Along with Georgia, No. 3 Alabama, No. 6 Texas, No. 8 Tennessee, and No. 11 Kentucky are all in CFP spots. No. 17 South Carolina is close by too, and Ole Miss (No. 19), LSU (No. 21), and Missouri are all ranked in the top 25 too. There was a lot of movement. Miami fell to No. 7 in the rankings after their loss to Notre Dame, which rose to No. 5. Kentucky fell to No. 11 after their loss to Tennessee, who rises to No. 8. Indiana drops five spots from No. 4 to No. 9 after winning against Minnesota, and BYU falls to No. 10 after losing to No. 2 Utah. As it stands, Georgia would get a first-round bye, since they're the No. 1 team in the country. top.title: Robert Griffin III makes emphatic Shedeur Sanders demand after Browns QB delivers 297-yard performance
top.description: Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images Robert Griffin III has called on the Cleveland Browns to make Shedeur Sanders their starting quarterback after the rookie impressed in his first NFL start against the New Orleans Saints. Sanders threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns despite being sacked five times as Cleveland suffered a narrow 23-22 overtime defeat. The performance came after Deshaun Watson had been under centre for the opening eight weeks of the season. Although the Browns came away without a win, Sanders gave them plenty to consider heading into Week 10. Griffin, a former Browns quarterback himself, believes the rookie has done enough to keep the starting job. Robert Griffin III believes Shedeur Sanders should have started for the Cleveland Browns all season Griffin was particularly impressed by Sanders’ ability to produce explosive plays and inspire his teammates despite having limited preparation during the week. Speaking about the rookie’s performance, RGIII made his position clear: “Fact! Scream it from the mountaintops. Shedeur Sanders should be the starting quarterback for the Cleveland Browns. Right, he gives the Browns explosive plays that Deshaun Watson hasn’t. Now I know Shedeur and the Browns lost their game in overtime, went for a two-point conversion and didn’t get it,” RGIII declared. He also questioned how Sanders could outperform the established starter despite not receiving the same number of practice repetitions. “But the way that he played and how he inspired the rest of his team, in my opinion, is why he should be the starting quarterback going forward. How does your backup, who doesn’t get any reps throughout the week, go out and outperform your starter? That, to me, is a sign that he should have been the starter from the beginning of the season.” However, Watson’s recent performances offer another side to the debate. The Browns quarterback threw for more than 300 yards in each of his two starts before Week 9. Sanders completed 19 of 31 passes against New Orleans without throwing an interception. Browns head coach Todd Monken praised his ability to deliver when the team needed him. “At the end, he came through when we needed him to come through with some big plays and big throws,” Monken said. With Cleveland yet to confirm its quarterback decision for Week 10, Sanders’ impressive debut has given the coaching staff a difficult choice to make. The Seattle Mariners ’ offseason plans have brought renewed attention to JP Crawford after the longtime shortstop completed his eighth season with the organization. Crawford reached free agency following the final season of the five-year extension he signed in April 2022. His tenure with the Mariners included a Gold Glove Award in 2020 and more appearances at shortstop than any player in franchise history. Acquired from the Philadelphia Phillies in December 2018, Crawford helped Seattle end its 21-year postseason drought in 2022. The Mariners have already made a substantial commitment to Colt Emerson, signing him to an eight-year, $95 million contract before his major league debut. nigeria.title: FG coming with major agric reforms to boost food production, cut inflation — ADENLE
nigeria.description: The Federal Government (FG) has proposed sweeping reforms in the agricultural sector, including digitalisation, mechanisation and improved coordination among government agencies in the sector, to boost food production, reduce food inflation and strengthen food security. Senior Special Adviser on Agricultural Innovation to the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security, Professor Ademola Adenle, disclosed this in an interview where he outlined plans to resolve long-standing challenges in the sector. Adenle said digitalisation will help government identify genuine farmers, monitor production, ensure transparent distribution of inputs and expand farmers’ access to markets. He said the National Agricultural Growth initiative had introduced a system where agro-dealers distribute inputs to verified farmers while monitoring their output. According to him, the intervention has increased production by 30%, with wheat output rising from 420,000 tonnes to 480,000 tonnes annually. He, however, admitted that higher production alone would not bring down food prices unless institutional weaknesses and structural inefficiencies were addressed. “Previous programmes focused mainly on production and input distribution without addressing institutional capacity, food security and agro-industrialisation,” he said. Adenle called for an overhaul of the ministry’s administrative and legal structures, noting that bureaucratic bottlenecks had limited the impact of interventions. He identified poor coordination among federal, state and local governments as a major challenge, and advocated harmonised agricultural policies across the three tiers. He also proposed performance-based financing, annual key performance indicators, stronger monitoring and evaluation, data-driven decision-making, and legislation to promote accountability and transparency. On rising food prices, Adenle blamed illegal movement of produce across Nigeria’s borders and hoarding of food commodities for creating artificial scarcity. He said the Nigeria Customs Service and the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission are working with security agencies to address the problem. nigeria.description: Dismisses alleged anti-Ngwa remark, cautions critics By Steve Oko UMUAHIA—Former Chief of Staff to ex-Governor Okezie Ikpeazu, Prof. ACB Agbazuere, who was a vocal critic of Governor Alex Otti during the 2019 governorship election, has declared support for the governor’s re-election bid, saying he deserves a second term. Agbazuere, now a member of Otti’s Campaign Advisory Council, also dismissed an allegation attributed to former Commissioner, Chief Charles Ogbonnaya, that the governor allegedly described Ngwa people as brainless, describing the claim as unfounded and politically motivated. Speaking during a radio interview simulcast across several stations in Abia on Tuesday, Agbazuere cautioned politicians against making unsubstantiated allegations, warning that defamatory statements could attract legal consequences under Nigerian laws, including the Cybercrimes Act. He said the allegation would not undermine Otti’s support base, particularly among the Ngwa people. “Dr Alex Otti may love peace; Dr Alex Otti may not want trouble, but they should see that people like us are now with him. nigeria.title: How AI is helping Nigerian farmers tackle crop diseases, improve farm decisions
nigeria.description: By Cynthia Alo With many Nigerian farmers still relying on traditional knowledge to identify crop diseases and determine appropriate treatments, delayed access to agricultural advice often means problems are left unresolved until they affect yields. In some cases, farmers have to wait days for agronomists to visit their farms and recommend solutions. CropCura, a digital agricultural innovation co-founded by Victor Onyekachukwu, is seeking to change this practice by bringing crop diagnosis and farm advisory services directly to farmers through technology. Onyekachukwu said the application allows farmers to take pictures of affected crops and receive an AI-powered analysis and recommendations on possible solutions in less than a minute. Apart from crop diagnosis, the platform provides weather information, an AI advisory service and digital farm mapping which allow farmers to access information needed to make decisions about their farms. He said the innovation also addresses another longstanding challenge in Nigerian agriculture which is farmers’ difficulty accessing formal credit because of inadequate records. Through digital farm profiles containing information about farmers, their locations, crops and farm sizes, Onyekachukwu said the technology will also combine a credit-scoring system that can help financial institutions assess farmers for lending. The platform, he said, currently has more than 2,000 farmers, who have mapped over 10,000 hectares of farmland. However, Onyekachukwu identified language barriers, limited smartphone access, low digital literacy and farmers’ distrust of technology as obstacles to wider adoption. He said the government should introduce policies recognising verified digital farm profiles as acceptable evidence for accessing agricultural loans and grants. nigeria.title: Research-policy disconnect undermines agric interventions — Experts
nigeria.description: By Cynthia Alo Agricultural experts have attributed the disconnect between farmers, researchers and policymakers as a major factor undermining the effectiveness of agricultural policies and interventions. This is even as they called for greater farmer participation in research design and policy formulation. According to them, research priorities were often determined without adequate consideration of farmers’ immediate needs, while policy implementation was constrained by funding limitations, institutional bottlenecks and poor communication of research findings. The experts spoke during the virtual inaugural episode of the Agricultural Policy Circle, organised by Farmosphere, with the theme, “Finding the Gap where Research, Policy, and Practice disconnect.” Agriculture researcher, Ifunanya Orisekeh,said research questions were sometimes determined before researchers reached farming communities, leaving farmers to respond to problems that might not reflect their immediate realities. She said research agendas were often shaped by funding calls, academic requirements and institutional timelines, while the time required to generate findings further widened the gap between research and practice. She said: “Research agendas are shaped before a funding call comes up. For example, if there is a project that needs a student already set, by the time you reach the field, the question is already printed and the farmer is there to answer your question. “So we can become very good in the research perspective. We are very good at answering questions that farmers have never asked.” Orisekeh said research could take three to four years to produce findings, by which time the conditions confronting farmers might have changed. She also questioned the practice of measuring project success by the number of farmers trained without establishing whether they continued using the recommended practices after project support ended. Using conservation agriculture as an example, she said, “It is widely promoted and many farmers have widely dropped it as well once the project and even the report is over.” She identified the mismatch between research schedules and farming seasons, inadequate representation of different categories of farmers and failure to return research findings to communities as other weaknesses. Also speaking, Founder of AgricIncome Hub and Chief Executive Officer of Maxipharo Farms, Olaoluwa Farotimi, identified inadequate access to credit, unstable markets, poor extension services, logistics challenges and climate-related risks as major constraints confronting farmers. He said agricultural financing often failed to reflect production cycles, while farmers had little control over market prices and could suffer losses from sudden policy changes. He said: “There is no access to credit for farmers. For example, you have a production cycle of two months or a month, and you have to pay back in six months while your crop is still in the field’’. nigeria.title: SMEs: NADF, Sahel Capital sign MoU to reduce borrowing costs
nigeria.description: By Gabriel Ewepu ABUJA – IN a bid to boost agribusiness, the National Agricultural Development Fund, NADF and Sahel Capital Fund Manager Limited have signed a Memorandum of Understanding, MoU, to expand access to affordable financing for Small and Medium Enterprises, SMEs, in the agricultural sector. The partnership which seeks to unlock more private-sector investments in agriculture, is expected to reduce the cost of borrowing for agribusinesses through innovative blended financing arrangements. Speaking at the signing ceremony, Executive Secretary, NADF, Muhammed Ibrahim, said the agreement marked a deliberate shift from conventional agricultural financing towards building an investment ecosystem capable of attracting sustainable capital into the sector. Ibrahim explained that NADF would bring its catalytic and development mandates, as well as its understanding of national agricultural priorities, to the partnership, while Sahel Capital would contribute investment expertise, market intelligence and experience across different agricultural value chains. According to him, the collaboration is designed to combine public-sector and concessionary capital with private investment expertise to unlock additional financing opportunities for viable agribusinesses. Under the MoU, both institutions will explore the feasibility of blended financing arrangements through which NADF provide funding alongside capital managed by Sahel Capital, including the Sahel Agribusiness Private Debt Fund, SAPDF. The proposed financing framework may feature risk-sharing mechanisms, concessional financing and other innovative funding structures aimed at improving access to capital for eligible agribusinesses. Sahel Capital is also expected to provide investment structuring, fund management and technical expertise, identify eligible agribusinesses and develop monitoring and reporting frameworks for the proposed facility. Other areas of collaboration include information sharing, development of a pipeline of bankable agribusiness projects, technical assistance and capacity building. Also speaking, Managing Partner, Sahel Capital, Mezuo Nwuneli, explained the partnership basically would help reduce borrowing costs for agribusiness SMEs by combining NADF funding with capital managed by the investment firm. However, Nwuneli lamented many agribusinesses currently obtain loans at interest rates ranging between 24 and 27 per cent, a situation he said makes business expansion, investment in productive capacity and long-term growth difficult. He said that the proposed collaboration would enable both institutions to provide financing at a lower blended cost, improving the financial viability of businesses and freeing up resources for expansion. nigeria.title: LASWA, Interferry complete ferry safety inspection training
nigeria.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni The Lagos State Waterways Authority (LASWA), in partnership with global trade association Interferry, has concluded Module 6 of the Africa Ferry Safety Development and Mentoring Programme to strengthen safety standards across the waterways sector. The training equipped maritime professionals with technical skills to audit and inspect commercial passenger ferries as part of efforts to improve passenger safety and compliance with international maritime standards. The module, titled “Survey and Inspection”, combined self-paced theoretical lessons from the American Bureau of Shipping (ABS) and Lloyd’s Register with virtual mentorship and practical field exercises. As part of the programme, participants attended a virtual “Ask the Expert” session on October 21 with Interferry specialists, Joep Bollerman, Francesco Ruisi and Darren Johnston, to discuss international ferry safety standards. This was followed by live condition and safety compliance audits at operational passenger ferry terminals, supervised by Sandra (Okoli) Ubong of ABS and Engr. Frank Fayinto of Lloyd’s Register. During the field exercises, participants applied an eight-step survey methodology covering preparation, onboard assessment and reporting. They were trained to identify safety deficiencies relating to hull integrity, life-saving appliances, fire protection systems and machinery, while applying the 5W+1H principle to ensure evidence-based reporting. The participants also learnt to classify identified risks into immediate, medium-term and low-priority interventions to facilitate timely corrective action. The initiative is supported by the Lagos State Government and the Special Adviser to the Governor on Blue Economy, Mr Oluwadamilola Emmanuel, alongside Interferry Chief Executive Officer, Mike Corrigan, and Ferrysafe Executive Sponsor, Shari Corrigan. With the successful completion of Module 6, the programme is expected to progress to Module 7, titled “Watchkeeping”, scheduled for November 2026. The next phase will further equip participating maritime professionals with competencies in vessel operations, navigational safety and effective watchkeeping practices. LASWA reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening professional standards, improving passenger safety and developing a more efficient, resilient and sustainable water transportation system in Lagos State and across Africa through international collaboration. This comes days after a renowned economist and former Governor of Nigeria’s Central Bank, Emir Muhammadu Sanusi, said he was impressed with the transformational feats recorded by Governor Dauda Lawal in the last three years in Zamfara State. The BudgIT report assesses the fiscal performance of 35 Nigerian states in 2025, the organisation said. “We call this ranking “Fiscal Viability”, but the real name is: Can your state survive without federal handouts?” the organisation said while releasing the report said. “States that rank higher on the Fiscal Viability pillar demonstrate a comparatively stronger capacity to manage their expenditure obligations within the limits of their available revenue,” BudgIT said in the new report. The report said Zamfara remained the second-least-indebted state in the federation, with a debt per capita of N19,464. Zamfara is one of the only three states from the northern part of the country that made it to the top 10 positions of the Fiscal Viability Index. The two other states are Gombe (78.07%) and Niger (76.03%), ranking 7th and 9th positions respectively. The report also examined how states generated revenue, managed public expenditure, sustained their finances and prioritised spending across critical sectors. The organisation said the 2026 assessment adopted a revised methodology built around four pillars: revenue performance (40 per cent), fiscal viability (30 per cent), debt sustainability (15 per cent) and spending on selected critical sectors (15 per cent). While commercial operations are picking up in some states, others continue to lag behind. For example, the Anambra State Government had to forcefully shut down markets in Onitsha and other areas to compel traders to reopen on Mondays, yet many businesses still remained closed. The exact reason for this hesitation remains unclear, as the threat of the sit-at-home order has significantly receded across the region, with the violent attacks and harassment of the past now seldom witnessed. However, findings indicate that many South-East residents have simply grown accustomed to this forced Monday routine after experiencing it for so long. Consequently, many individuals—particularly independent business owners—now voluntarily choose to rest on Mondays. Furthermore, several rural communities have permanently adopted Mondays for communal meetings, neighbourhood policing, road repairs, and other civic activities. Ultimately, what began as a forced restriction has largely transitioned into a voluntary day of rest, effectively extending the weekend by an extra day.In Aba, Abia State, following disruptions associated with the Monday sit-at-home, major markets in the commercial city are yet to fully recover their usual Monday patronage. nigeria.title: Kebbi APC reconciles aggrieved members ahead of 2027 polls
nigeria.description: By Haruna Aliyu, Birnin Kebbi The All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kebbi State has declared that it is united and strong ahead of the 2027 general elections, following a reconciliation exercise aimed at addressing grievances among party members. The Secretary of the Contact and Reconciliation Committee set up by Governor Nasir Idris, Engineer Ahmed Umar Faruk, made this known on Tuesday in Birnin Kebbi while briefing journalists on the committee’s activities. According to him, the committee recorded significant progress by providing a platform for aggrieved members to express their concerns and ensuring that their complaints received attention. world.title: Teddy Riner candidacy 'illustrative of this hunger for an alternative' to Le Pen or Mélenchon
world.description: As Teddy Riner throws his hat in the race for the French presidency, amid France's sociopolitical and economic crises. François Picard is pleased to welcome Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence at at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University. The prospect of Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner entering France's presidential race raises questions that extend well beyond the political ambitions of a celebrated athlete. At a time when traditional parties are struggling to mobilize voters and the political center remains deeply fragmented, Riner's emergence points to a broader transformation in democratic competition: the growing importance of personal credibility, public visibility and the capacity to embody an alternative to established political elites. In an interview with France 24, Lex Paulson, Professor of Collective Intelligence at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University, argues that the changing relationship between voters and political institutions is reshaping the conditions under which political outsiders can emerge. "The currency of politics now is no longer just money to buy television advertisements or open offices. It's the ability to capture attention." For Paulson, Riner's celebrity status gives him a considerable advantage in an increasingly fragmented media environment. Yet visibility alone does not confer political credibility. While the Olympic champion's public commitments against racism and xenophobia may resonate with voters, Paulson questions whether he has articulated a sufficiently developed political vision to become a serious presidential contender. The deeper issue, however, is not whether Riner can win. It is what his potential candidacy reveals about the weakness of France's traditional political alternatives and the growing demand for leaders whose personal histories, values and commitments resonate with citizens. "Voters don't vote for policies. Voters vote for people they sense will stand up for them." Paulson's analysis connects this demand for political identification to a wider crisis of democratic representation. Voters, he suggests, increasingly perceive professional politicians as a distant governing class that listens to citizens only during electoral campaigns. "People don't feel like they're being listened to except for the few weeks before an election." Seen in this light, Riner's emergence is less an isolated celebrity phenomenon than a symptom of the changing relationship between political authority, public trust and democratic participation. The central challenge facing France's next generation of leaders may therefore be not simply to develop compelling policies, but to restore citizens' sense that political institutions are responsive to their lives. As Paulson concludes, the real political opportunity lies in reimagining governance itself: bringing decision-making closer to citizens and giving them a more meaningful voice in the democratic process.

House Bill 815, filed by Rep. Ron Reynolds, a Missouri City Democrat, on the first day of prefiling for the 90th Texas Legislature, carries the caption “Relating to the authority of a municipality or county to invest money in cryptocurrencies.” The introduced text , posted on the Texas Legislature’s site, is two sections long. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Poland’s Parliament Votes 240-202 to Let Officials Freeze Crypto Before Court Review Poland’s lower house of parliament voted 240-202 on Friday to let the interior minister freeze crypto assets, bank accounts and other property of people placed on a national sanctions list, before any court reviews the order. The Sejm, Poland’s lower house, passed the Act on Restrictive Measures at its 68th sitting, with one member abstaining and 17 not voting. The Senate received the bill Monday and has 30 days under Article 121 of the Constitution to adopt, amend or reject it, after which it would go to President Karol Nawrocki. The law, a government bill that also implements European Union sanctions rules, treats crypto assets as financial means that can be frozen, using the definition in the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation. A freeze, as the text defines it, is meant to stop any movement, transfer, use or other change that would let the holder benefit from the assets. The freeze applies only to people and entities the interior minister adds to a public national list, either on the minister’s own initiative or at the request of agencies that include the financial watchdog, the central bank, the financial intelligence unit and the internal security service. Grounds include supporting a country already under EU sanctions, serious human rights abuses, or initiating or financing information manipulation that poses a serious threat to Poland’s national security. A listing on that last ground requires a showing of a real and serious threat to Poland’s interests, borders, security or elections. The bill carves out ordinary journalism, political speech and publishing, unless that activity is a knowing campaign of the kind the law describes. A freeze that starts before a judge weighs in The interior minister’s decision takes effect the day after it is posted in the ministry’s Public Information Bulletin and is immediately enforceable. There is no request to the minister to reconsider. A listed person may file a complaint with an administrative court, but the law says the decision remains in force until a judgment becomes final, and it sets aside the usual rule that would let a court pause a challenged order. The measures also bar making funds or property available to listed persons and can exclude them from public contracts. In some cases, the economy minister may appoint a temporary administrator to sell frozen assets or, under a separate order, take them over for the State Treasury. Speaking on the theme “Losing the Fear” , at The International Women Leadership Conference (TIWLC) in Dubai, organised by the Ibukun Awosika Leadership Foundation, Ekeh , who was a keynote speaker on the final day of this year’s conference, addressed over 600 women industry leaders from different countries across the globe. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. Bamboo, sisal, reeds, and sedge are used in basketry, and she breeds Angora goats for their fur, which she straightens and dyes to make garments. Cowhide obtained from local abattoirs is softened in a tannery before being mixed into leather designs. “I keep Angora goats for the fur needed in garment production. However, for raw materials such as cowhide, I usually source these from local abattoirs while sisal and tree barks are either harvested by me or sometimes extracted by colleagues I work with, who are based in the rural areas.” Desmond Ntini , a cultural entrepreneur based in Bulawayo, sees Malunga’s work as part of a broader shift in how African history is perceived and used. ” Malunga is redefining the fashion industry by blending traditional African influences with contemporary creativity. sports.description: EUGENE — One of Oregon football’s most important defensive players is done for the season. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. sports.title: Stephen A. Smith says Lakers can’t win a title with ‘top three players being white’
sports.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images The Los Angeles Lakers have been one of the NBA’s best teams to start the season, winning six straight games behind Luka Doncic. But Stephen A. Smith still isn’t buying them as a championship contender for a rather bizarre reason: their top players are all white. This week, the ESPN star claimed that he wasn’t sold on the Lakers winning a championship, pointing to the race of their top players. Smith said that he has “never seen an NBA team with its top three players being white” win a championship, and that “it ain’t gonna happen” this year. Lakers’ Hot Start The Lakers retooled their roster around Doncic this offseason. Along with Austin Reaves, they added center Walker Kessler in a July sign-and-trade with the Utah Jazz, sending multiple future first-round picks and pick swaps to Utah. The move has paid off so far. The Lakers have won six straight games, with Doncic putting up 32 points, eight rebounds, and 10 assists in his return to the lineup in a win over the Atlanta Hawks, per ESPN . Smith made a similar argument about the Lakers’ big three over the summer, and the comments drew plenty of backlash at the time. ‘It ain’t gonna happen’ While the Lakers may be off to a hot start this season, Smith made it clear that he hasn’t changed his mind. “I’ve never seen an NBA team with its top three players being white deliver a championship. It’s never happened. And I’m here to tell you, I don’t think it’s gonna happen this year,” Smith said, in a clip shared by Awful Announcing . After running through other contenders, Smith added, “Lakers got a chance. I just don’t think it’s going to materialize into a championship.” Smith insisted that he wasn’t making an issue of race, but was “just talking about the actual facts.” He then ran through a list of past champions, from the Larry Bird and Kevin McHale Boston Celtics to the Golden State Warriors. “You can bring up whoever the hell you want. There has never been in my lifetime an NBA team led with its top three players being white that delivered you a championship with an abundance of brothers playing basketball,” Smith said. Smith admitted that a title for Doncic would be big for the NBA, especially with the Olympics coming to Los Angeles in 2028. “It would be huge for the league. It would be huge for the Olympics. It would be huge for LA. It would be huge for everything, but it ain’t gonna happen. I can’t see it,” Smith said. “Not a team with its top three players being white dudes. I’m sorry, I think that’s controversial in some people’s eyes. It ain’t controversial in mine. I’m just telling you how it is. sports.title: Hawks fall short in OT to Virginia Tech, 93-88
sports.description: SIOUX CITY, IOWA - NOVEMBER 10: Cooper Koch #8 of the Iowa Hawkeyes drives against Amani Hansberry #13 of the Virginia Tech Hokies during the second half at Tyson Events Center on November 10, 2026 in Sioux City, Iowa. (Photo by Steven Branscombe/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Iowa Hawkeyes (2-1) got slow starts in each of the three frames tonight in a 93-88 loss to Virginia Tech (3-0). The most notable was not scoring a field goal until 0:44 left in the overtime frame. Despite having a chance to tie at the end, Cooper Koch couldn’t make his 3 point attempt amidst a career night. Giving up 93 points is never Ben McCollum’s preferred style and they struggled to contain the Hokie guards, Ben Hammond & Jaylen Curry, who combined for 57 points on 18/34 shooting and 16/18 from the line. Curry’s 3 pointer in overtime proved to be enough distance for Tech as the Hawks couldn’t get it inside of 2 after that. It was a game riddled with fouls and the Hawks finished 66% (31/47) from the line. The biggest of which was Ty’reek Coleman missing on his final attempt with less than 2 seconds left in regulation. Andrew McKeever couldn’t convert the putback quick enough, which allowed VT to come away with the victory in Sioux City’s Tyson Center. The flipside of foul trouble was Kael Combs who lived in foul trouble for the bulk of the game with 2 early ones before the first television timeout, a third later in the first half, and a fourth right out of the break. Thankfully Coleman performed well off the bench with 20 points on 7/10 shooting. Career night for Cooper Koch Despite missing his final attempt of the game, Koch was aggressive all night, with 15/17 from the line en route to a career high 26 points. He was just 5/11 from the field and 1/5 from 3 but he played incredibly hard for all 45 minutes of the game. Many of his free throw attempts came on drives and post ups where he pulled out the Kevin Durant rip throw. Iowa will need to see him take more shots. Koch was joined in double digits by Coleman, Isaia Howard (13 on 3/5 from deep), and Combs (10 points on 4/4). Offensive rebounding kept the Hawks in it Iowa rebounded 18 of 35 opportunities, good for 18 second chance points. It came from unexpected sources – McKeever got his 3 but Coleman and Howard added 3 of their own. While Iowa went after size in the portal, much of the rebounding gains tonight happened from Iowa’s guards. High leverage free throw shooting hurts Iowa Coleman missed the second of 2 attempts down the stretch and then he & Koch combined for 3/5 in the extra frame. Any one of those misses very easily could have flipped it for Iowa. Overall the 31/47 is going to add some frustration to the loss but 7 of Iowa’s 16 misses came from Cam Manyawu & McKeever who went just 2/9. They’re not good FT shooters but they have to be better than that. Next up: Sunday, November 15th at 2:00p vs Creighton in Des Moines, IA

sports.title: UCLA football makes stunning move in CFP rankings after initial snub
sports.description: Given another week to assess UCLA, the College Football Playoff selection committee had a different take on the Bruins. Move them up. Way up. In the wake of an impressive road victory over Minnesota, UCLA rose to No. 4 in the CFP rankings released Tuesday night. That’s four spots above where the Bruins were slotted only a week ago . Most importantly, moving into the top four puts UCLA (9-0 overall, 6-0 Big Ten) on track to receive a first-round bye into the quarterfinal round of the 12-team playoff. UCLA running back Wayne Knight (3) celebrates after scoring a touchdown against Minnesota in an NCAA college football game Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, in Minneapolis. AP Photo/Abbie Parr So, did the CFP selection committee make a mistake last week when it came to the Bruins? “I don’t think it was an admission of them being ranked too low,” Hunter Yurachek, chairman of the CFP selection committee, said on a conference call with reporters. “I think what we’re seeing with the parity around college football [is] that we now have only two remaining unbeaten teams and UCLA is one of those, and I think they continue to improve as a team. “The defense has been steady and really dominant all season, they’ve had an established running game and their quarterback play is getting better — their backup quarterback that has been filling in really seemed to find his way, especially in the fourth quarter of that game against Minnesota.” Notre Dame wide receiver Micah Gilbert (14) scores a touchdown during the second half of an NCAA college football game against Miami, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026. AP Photo/Paul Barnick Yurachek was alluding to quarterback Ty Dieffenbach, who replaced the injured Nico Iamaleava a month ago, throwing 75-yard touchdown passes on back-to-back offensive plays to help the Bruins pull away for a 34-20 victory over the Golden Gophers. This is UCLA’s highest spot ever in the CFP rankings after its No. 8 ranking last week tied its previous high from the 2014 season. The only teams ranked ahead of the Bruins were No. 1 Georgia, No. 2 Utah and No. 3 Alabama. UCLA and Utah are the last remaining unbeaten teams in major college football. The Bruins’ move was part of a major shakeup in which no team remained in the same CFP spot as a week ago. USC (7-2, 4-2) rose two spots to No. 18 and has a chance to vastly improve its standing Saturday when it faces No. 9 Indiana, which dropped five spots despite not playing last weekend. Should the Bruins secure a first-round bye, they’ll need to come up with a plan to avoid the fate of nearly every predecessor in that spot — teams with byes have gone only 1-7 in the quarterfinals since the playoff expanded to 12 teams for the 2024 season. sports.title: Robert Griffin III makes emphatic Shedeur Sanders demand after Browns QB delivers 297-yard performance
sports.description: Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images Robert Griffin III has called on the Cleveland Browns to make Shedeur Sanders their starting quarterback after the rookie impressed in his first NFL start against the New Orleans Saints. Sanders threw for 297 yards and two touchdowns despite being sacked five times as Cleveland suffered a narrow 23-22 overtime defeat. The performance came after Deshaun Watson had been under centre for the opening eight weeks of the season. Although the Browns came away without a win, Sanders gave them plenty to consider heading into Week 10. Griffin, a former Browns quarterback himself, believes the rookie has done enough to keep the starting job. Robert Griffin III believes Shedeur Sanders should have started for the Cleveland Browns all season Griffin was particularly impressed by Sanders’ ability to produce explosive plays and inspire his teammates despite having limited preparation during the week. Speaking about the rookie’s performance, RGIII made his position clear: “Fact! Scream it from the mountaintops. Shedeur Sanders should be the starting quarterback for the Cleveland Browns. Right, he gives the Browns explosive plays that Deshaun Watson hasn’t. Now I know Shedeur and the Browns lost their game in overtime, went for a two-point conversion and didn’t get it,” RGIII declared. He also questioned how Sanders could outperform the established starter despite not receiving the same number of practice repetitions. “But the way that he played and how he inspired the rest of his team, in my opinion, is why he should be the starting quarterback going forward. How does your backup, who doesn’t get any reps throughout the week, go out and outperform your starter? That, to me, is a sign that he should have been the starter from the beginning of the season.” However, Watson’s recent performances offer another side to the debate. The Browns quarterback threw for more than 300 yards in each of his two starts before Week 9. Sanders completed 19 of 31 passes against New Orleans without throwing an interception. Browns head coach Todd Monken praised his ability to deliver when the team needed him. “At the end, he came through when we needed him to come through with some big plays and big throws,” Monken said. With Cleveland yet to confirm its quarterback decision for Week 10, Sanders’ impressive debut has given the coaching staff a difficult choice to make. After failed negotiations with several other opponents, Paro stepped up to face the pound-for-pound ranked Haney. We get it. Liam Paro isn’t Ryan Garcia, Shakur Stevenson, or Keyshawn Davis. But when matchup after matchup for three-division world champion and top pound-for-pound welterweight Devin Haney fell through this year, credit the IBF World Welterweight champion Liam Paro of Australia for taking the unification fight with the WBO World Welterweight champion on his home turf in San Francisco just before the Christmas holiday. On Tuesday, the Claudefather announced Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards, and Claude Data, and promised the imminent arrival of Claude Meetings. These artifact types join existing ones – Docs, Slides, Design, and Motion – to form a nascent Claude-dependent productivity suite. Anthropic initially used the term artifacts to refer to shareable AI-based interactive tools, like dynamic charts. But the scope of the term has been stretched to cover specific artifact types, which refer to what traditionalists might take to mean files associated with specific hosted applications. "An artifact is anything Claude makes for you that you'd put in front of someone: a design, a deck, a document, a dashboard, or a small interactive tool," the company explains. The key thing that distinguishes an artifact from a file is that users are meant to interact with artifacts through Claude, rather than storing and transferring them independently. Think of it more as a container or managed object that opens in Claude (via a sharing URL), because artifacts in fact consist of various content types – .txt, .md, .html, .jsx, .svg, .pptx, .docx, .zip, .pdf, and .mp4, among others. Anthropic's vision of Claude as a container for other applications goes beyond artifacts. The AI biz has also expanded its interactive connectors , which turn Claude into a landlord for other software applications. Its own promotional video for the feature hammers that point home in its title: " Your apps have moved into Claude ." "Starting today, partners can embed their apps directly in Claude, so you can work in Adobe, Atlassian, and others without switching tabs," Anthropic said. technology.title: Ye olde server consolidation has made Cisco push top-of-rack switching to 100G
technology.description: Server consolidation has led Cisco to boost the speed of top-of-rack switches to 100G. The networking giant last week announced the catchily named N9348C8D-H2, a 1U device packing 48 100G SFP-DD ports and eight 400G QSFP-DD uplinks. At the Cisco Live event in Melbourne, Australia, this week, Cisco’s senior veep for datacenter and internet infrastructure, Kevin Wollenweber, said one reason the company created the device is that modern servers often feature a pair of fast network interface cards. The twin cards are needed because sixth-gen server processors from Intel and AMD offer dozens, or even hundreds, of physical processor cores and therefore generate a lot of traffic. The density of computing power those processors provide has led chipmakers and server manufacturers to suggest replacing handfuls of machines running older, power-guzzling Xeons and Epycs with boxes running more efficient sixth-gen chips. The Register hears it’s not uncommon to achieve 6:1 server consolidation ratios when moving from third- or fourth-generation Xeons or Epycs to current models. Users who make that move can pack many more server cores into the same rack. Power bills go down, but the quantity of data leaving a rack goes up. Wollenweber said Cisco realized it had “tons” of switches that offer 25G ports but felt it had a gap in its range for non-AI scenarios like server consolidation that produced increased data flows. The exec admitted that the 100G ports may be overkill for a modest collection of new servers, but argued users recognize it won’t be long before they grow into the excess capacity – perhaps as they use more agentic AI applications. Cisco sees traffic from AI agents stressing the north-south connections that link organizations to the cloud and also driving much more east-west traffic across internal networks. At Cisco Live, the company’s execs suggested that network upgrades are therefore an inevitable necessity. That’s not entirely self-serving, because agents will vastly outnumber humans and constantly create traffic, compared to the flurries of network activity that happen when humans use generative AI or chatbots. Cisco argues that deploying agents at scale will therefore only be possible on highly automated networks. “Humans can no longer comprehend the amount of data that we actually have in a network,” Wollenweber told The Register . Cisco’s Canvas agentic operations platform aims to at least make humans aware when their attention is needed, by detecting problems and offering to make repairs. Joe Vaccaro, Cisco’s senior vice president and general manager for Network Platform and Assurance, told The Register he believes network administrators don’t feel threatened by suggestions from AI agents when they concern familiar, routine, low-risk tasks that IT pros are confident the agents can handle. Over time, he said, networking pros will learn to trust agents with more complex work. ®

The group’s web page points out, “Certified Kubernetes tests the cluster, and Kubernetes AI Conformance tests whether a cluster can run AI and ML workloads. Nothing comparable exists for the workloads themselves, so cluster operators still check each application by hand before routine maintenance or a Kubernetes upgrade. Every cluster operator ends up repeating the same assessment, and application maintainers get the same questions from each environment they support,” the group asserts. technology.description: It’s another doozy of a Patch Tuesday, with Microsoft fixing 1,094 bugs in its products, including one that attackers exploited before Redmond released a patch. Jake Knott, head of threat intelligence at exposure management firm watchTowr, succinctly said in an email to The Register : “Maybe we should just go home.” “Most security teams haven’t quite recovered from the last month of bumper-to-bumper critical vulnerabilities, emergency patches, and ‘2shell’-branded everything, and we’re yet again at another Patch Tuesday,” Knott told us. Starting with the zero-day: It’s an Outlook spoofing vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-124194 , and it only garnered a 6.5 out of 10 CVSS rating. But as Dustin Childs, head of threat awareness at TrendAI’s Zero Day Initiative, warns, don’t let the score or the name lull you into thinking it’s OK to put off patching this one. “It’s labeled spoofing, but the impact is bigger than the name suggests,” Childs said in his monthly Patch Tuesday review . “An attacker sends a specially crafted message file and convinces a user to open it,” he wrote. “Outlook then connects to an attacker-controlled network location without showing the usual external-content warning, which discloses the user’s NTLMv2 hash. The attacker can use that hash to authenticate as the user.” Microsoft marked CVE-2026-124194 as exploited, but per usual didn’t say when the attacks started, who is battering this bug, and what they are doing with the access post exploitation. These details will likely start trickling out soon. Plus, now that there’s a public fix, other miscreants are undoubtedly already scanning for vulnerable versions and reverse engineering the patch for their own attack purposes. So prioritize this fix, and keep an eye on your inbox for any suspicious files. Back-to-back months of 1K+ CVEs Despite the second month of more than 1,000 CVEs (October had 1,474 ), CVE-2026-124194 is the only one under active exploitation, and none of the 1,094 are listed as publicly known. Childs says this shouldn’t give organizations “false comfort.” “Logging back-to-back months above 1,000 CVEs proves automated bug-hunting has permanently reset patch volume,” he told The Register . “With AI making patch-diffing and exploit generation near-instant, the threat window opens the minute these updates drop.” For defenders, this means two things, Childs added. “What defenders need to know and do right now is abandon broad triage and take immediate defensive action: patch Exchange and Domain Controllers (LDAP/Kerberos) first to stop zero-click compromise, ring-fence exposed network services like DNS and DHCP to prevent wormable spread, and verify manual administrative fixes on your cloud services,” he said. science.title: SpaceX moves Starship Flight 15 booster to launch pad for 'squeeze test' ahead of epic double-catch attempt (photos)
science.description: null SpaceX is one big step closer to the 15th test flight of its Starship megarocket. The company announced today (Nov. 10) that it had moved its latest Starship first stage, known as Super Heavy Booster 22, to the launch mount at its Starbase facility in South Texas ahead of Flight 15, which is scheduled to lift off this Friday (Nov. 13). During the upcoming launch test, SpaceX plans to catch both Booster 22 and Starship's Ship upper stage with its launch tower's "chopstick" arms in a double landing catch — something the private spaceflight company has never tried before. It will be the first full recovery of an orbital rocket in history. SpaceX's Flight 15 Starship Super Heavy booster in its assembly bay, before its move to Starbase's launch mount. (Image credit: SpaceX) Booster 22 therefore "was used for final catch testing upon arrival [at the pad], including a suspended squeeze test at catch height," SpaceX said in an X post today (Nov. 10). That post shared four photos of the giant booster, which is powered by 33 of SpaceX's next-gen Raptor engines. The first shot showed Super Heavy in one of Starbase's "Mega Bay" assembly buildings before rollout, while the other three depicted it grasped by the tower's arms, held high in the South Texas sky. SpaceX will try to catch both Super Heavy and Ship during Flight 15 — something it's never done before. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has used the chopstick arms during Starship flights before; it has successfully caught Super Heavy on three separate occasions. But the company has never attempted a catch of Ship, which flies higher and farther than the booster and is therefore a more challenging target. And SpaceX only reached orbit with Starship for the first time on Flight 14, which launched on Sept. 28. So Flight 15 will break new ground. And, if all goes to plan, it will give us a look at the future: SpaceX plans to catch Super Heavy and Ship on all operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will allow the company to boost the megarocket's launch cadence. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 10, 2013: Europe's GOCE satellite, the 'Ferrari of space,' fell out of orbit after mapping Earth's gravity field
science.description: null On Nov. 10, 2013, Europe's GOCE satellite fell to Earth after four years in orbit mapping the planet's gravitational field. GOCE, its name was short for Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer, launched in 2009 on a mission to map Earth's gravity like never before. But despite that successful mission, it was doomed in 2013 when it ran out of fuel . At the time, controllers weren't sure where GOCE would fall back to Earth . Some people worried that it might crash into a populated area. However, the small spacecraft broke up in the atmosphere and didn't cause any property damage. It disintegrated about 50 miles above the Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic Ocean. The European Space Agency called the mission a success. GOCE lasted far longer than expected. It showed small variations in Earth's gravity , mapped the structure of Earth's crust and mantle, and tracked ocean currents. Artist's rendering of the "Ferrari of space," the European Space Agency's Gravity field and steady-state Ocean Circulation Explorer (GOCE), before it fell from space in 2013. (Image credit: European Space Agency) Why it mattered The GOCE satellite was a sleek spacecraft, with fins covered in solar panels that gave it a futuristic design. In fact, its look earned it a pretty cool nickname. "GOCE's sleek, elegant aerodynamic design — responsible for it being dubbed the 'Ferrari of space' — immediately set it apart from most other satellites,." ESA officials said in a description . There was more than looks behind GOCE's design. In order to generate the best map ever of Earth's gravitational field, GOCE had to fly in an orbit so low — just 139 miles (224 kilometers) — it needed to counteract the drag from the gossamer thin atmosphere of Earth at that altitude. The International Space Station orbits Earth at nearly twice that altitude. GOCE was powered by an xenon ion engine that allowed to maintain its low orbit for four years. Once it ran out of fuel, the 1-ton satellite could not maintain its position in space , leading to a fiery plunge to Earth. The large size of GOCE — it weighed 2,425 pounds (1,100 kilograms) and was 17 feet (5.3 meters) long and 3.2 feet (1 m) wide — made its reentry stand out, particularly since at least 25% of the satellite was expected to reach the Earth's surface . science.title: A distant exoplanet mysteriously vanished from sight. Astronomers just discovered why
science.description: null Astronomers have solved the mystery of an extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, that "disappeared" after seven years of observations. New research suggests that the planet hasn't vanished at all, but has been dragged off its orbit by an unseen planet. The exoplanet , designated TOI-2535 b, is located around 1,000 light-years away. TOI-2535 b was routinely observed with NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite ( TESS ) space telescope for seven years between April 2019 and March 2026 as it completed its 8.25-Earth day orbit of its parent star. That's 10 times quicker than the orbit of Mercury around the sun and means this blisteringly hot planet is classed as a " hot Jupiter ." However, something strange happened started to happen as astronomers observed the distant world. The orbits of the planet weren't regular like those of other planets, with TOI-2535 b often arriving six hours early or six hours later than when astronomers expected. Then, in March this year, TESS was no longer spotting the characteristic drops in starlight that TOI-2535 b caused as it crossed, or "transited," the face of its parent star. It seemed to have vanished. This team used TESS data to determine that TOI-2535 b is being pulled on by an unseen neighbor and is, in turn, pulling on that planet as well. This is causing the orbits of both worlds in the TOI-2535 system to "wobble." TOI-2535 b disappeared when that wobble tilted it out of alignment with its star. "We think of the universe as resembling clockwork, where everything is regular, but that's not true. If there are multiple planets in a system, they can affect each other's orbits. We know of a few systems that are like this," team member Samuel Yee of the University of California, Los Angeles, said in a statement . "This is the most extreme example we've seen because the two planets are interacting so strongly. The planet's orbit is tilting so quickly that its transit disappeared while we were watching." TOI-2535 b isn't expected to transit its parent star for at least 30 years, but the hidden neighbor tugging on it may cross the face of the star sooner than that. In the meantime, scientists will attempt to decode what this extreme wobbling exoplanet system says about how it formed. Hot Jupiters should be cool customers There is currently a lot of speculation about how hot Jupiter planets like TOI-2535 b form. That is because current routes of planet formation suggest planets like this would need to form around a great deal of ice. Obviously, ice isn't likely to be abundant as close to a star as TOI-2535 b is currently. This means that hot Jupiters likely form far from their stars and then migrate inwards . There are two ways that this could happen. The planet could be excited into an elliptical orbit by violent events like a near-collision with another planetary object, and then interactions with the star pull the planet inwards. Alternatively, the hot Jupiter may be pulled inwards along with the other planets
